corrected_blocks.text: He will reign. The glory of His kingdom, the holiness of His course, will be apparent to all when He completes His work and will reign. He will fold up the skies and unfold new skies on the day appointed by lot for Him from Zion to reign. The nations falter, the proud clamour, the arrogant fall when the exalted One comes to reign. Then those compared to the fish of the sea (Israel) shall rule, their multitude will be raised up when the King of nations comes forth to reign. The noblest of the peoples shall be gathered from among the peoples to bring the smallest of peoples to their place where He will reign. They will chant pleasant songs before them whom He has lifted up from among the peoples so that over them He may reign. The idols of Sikkut, the abominations
On the Sabbath.

As it is written in Thy Torah: He was King in Yeshurun when the heads of the people assembled together with the tribes of Israel. Make for Thyself in Zion an awe-inspiring name, prosper it as of old with the throne of the kingdom. Arouse and revive the delight of the whole earth (Jerusalem) and establish Thy throne in the city of the kingdom. As it is written in Thy holy words: a beautiful branch, the delight of the whole earth, the mountain of Zion, the stronghold of the North, the city of the great King. The light of the moon and of the sun wilt Thou cause to blush and those who worship them will be put to shame when Thou dost lift up the kingdom. Glorify the city of beauty, that it may be bright as the sun and reveal in front of us the glory of the kingdom. As it is written through Thy prophet: and the moon shall blush and the sun be ashamed, for the Lord of Hosts rules on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem and in front of His elders there is glory.
changes: Text agrees with the print. The Hebrew linkage catchwords (ככתוב, עשה, ככתוב, פני, ככתוב) are left out of the prayer text and recorded under source_boundaries.

corrected_blocks.text: of Kiyun, are dragged along as if slain, they are cast down so that they may not reign. O assembly of the Supreme God, do homage, you sons of the powerful (forefathers), offer singing and praise to the Lord for He will reign. When He lifts His strong hand to raise up His prince and exalts those He has carried, He will be powerful and reign. When He raises His hand above the high heavens, on the splendour of His throne He will be seated and reign. The earth is shaken by destruction and ruin, in which dwellers on earth will be ensnared when He will rage and reign. Three times will He make sound the dread of powerful Shofar blasts and them will He favour, they will cause glory to rise from the end of the earth, for He will reign. Beauty from the earth will ascend and glory from the sea, exultation from the heavens above, they will all rejoice when He will reign. To the hosts of all creatures He brings remedy for their defects, aloud will they praise His glory: Behold in justice does He reign. The princes
On Sabbath.

The hosts redeemed from Egypt sang on the night of the feast, this is the night preserved for the devastation of a kingdom; they stepped through the waters of the sea, they looked with a spirit of insight to the place where they were to be planted and receive the kingdom. As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘Thou wilt bring them and plant them upon the mount of Thine inheritance, the site for Thy dwelling which Thou hast made, O Lord, the sanctuary, O Lord, which Thy hands have established’. And it was said: ‘The Lord will reign for ever and ever’. Destroyed are the gates of the temple, the House of eternity, for there has ceased from among them the Kingdom. The Holy One will return to them for ever; then will they raise their heads again when He renews the kingdom. As it is written: ‘Lift up your heads, O gates, and lift yourselves up, O portals of eternity, so that the King of glory may enter. Who is this King of glory? He is the Lord, mighty and strong, the Lord, mighty in war’. And it was said: ‘Lift up your heads, O gates, lift up, O portals of eternity, so that the King of glory may enter. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of Hosts, He is the King of glory, Selah’.
changes: 'renews the Kingdom'→'renews the kingdom' (lowercase as printed)
Catchwords (צבאות, ככתוב, קמטו, ככתוב) left out of the prayer text

source_boundaries: Weekday piyyut (above the rule): it continues from an earlier page into s266 and ends mid-phrase on כִּיּוּן. s268 picks up with גִּלּוּלִים, so the end of s266 is a running word, not a catchword, and nothing is duplicated. s268 ends at יַשְׁלִיכוּ., and the stanza continues on the next Hebrew page.

Shabbat piyyut (below the rule) is kept separate from the weekday piyyut. s266 has the rubric, verse, stanza ע, verse, stanza פ, verse. s268 has the rubric, stanza צ, verse, stanza ק, verse. Each stanza is split in two by a printed role abbreviation (ח׳ or א׳, unresolved), which is kept as its own speaker block.
Neither Hebrew page has a printed catchword at the foot. The running headers (page 123/124, מוּסַף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה) are left out.
The English Shabbat paragraphs begin with Hebrew linkage catchwords. s267: ככתוב, עשה, ככתוב, פני, ככתוב. s269: צבאות, ככתוב, קמטו, ככתוב. These are navigation cues, not prayer text.
